summary: Isolate a Claude seat's channel and hooks from nested Claude processes, and retain automatic channel-recovery attempts across brief replacement success.

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection rebuild.

schema.detail: No database schema, replicated claim format or migration changes. New controlled Claude generations retain an additive local process-generation witness alongside their existing harness ownership.

rules.detail: No claim vocabulary or admission-rule change. Existing fenced runtime actions and mailbox epochs remain in use.

compatibility.detail: Nested channels serve an unscoped MCP protocol and cannot bind a protected primary seat; nested hooks cannot publish its native-session or observation state. Nested-Claude isolation is restart-gated: it protects only wrappers started after the upgrade. Existing wrapper generations without a witness retain legacy admission until their next natural authorized restart; doctor reports those seats as unprotected, so upgrading a daemon alone does not protect the whole fleet. Old daemons ignore the additive witness. The automatic replacement start reason now identifies automatic recovery instead of explicit intent; mixed fleets retain the old reason text from old members.

manual.detail: No agent conduct, environment stripping, configuration or tool restrictions are required.

recovery.detail: Automatic success does not erase attempts. Three attempts within a persisted rolling six-hour window park channel recovery with its existing owner-visible fault; explicit authorized restart or expiry reopens the budget. Parking targets only its recorded incarnation. Existing explicit restart and required deployment paths remain available.

downtime.detail: Source qualification does not authorize interrupting an active seat or establish installed-process remediation. Kernel and synthetic controls require ordinary hosted qualification.
